content.content:
AST-aware code search for TypeScript, JavaScript and Rust.
Built for AI coding agents, not humans reading a terminal.

> **Status: early.** `monokl search` works today for TypeScript, JavaScript and Rust. Symbol lookup, references, definitions and dependents are designed (see [`docs/spec/`](docs/spec/README.md)) but not built yet. --- ## What you get Grep finds text. Embeddings find _vibes_. monokl parses your code with a compiler-grade parser ([OXC](https://oxc.rs) for TypeScript and JavaScript, [rust-analyzer's syntax crate](https://crates.io/crates/ra_ap_syntax) for Rust), so a search returns the **function, class, struct, trait or type** that matches, not a line number to open and read. - **Whole code units, best first.** Results are ranked, with functions, classes and methods ahead of imports and re-exports. A search for `format price` puts `formatCurrency` and `validatePrice` first, because names are split on `camelCase`, `snake_case` and acronyms before matching. A block whose own name holds query words ranks above one that only uses them in its body. - **A small query language.** Plain words, `"quoted phrases"`, `+required` and `-excluded` terms, and `regex:` patterns. See [Writing a query](#writing-a-query). - **Your project's rules apply.** Files that `.gitignore` or `.ignore` exclude, hidden files, test files, Rust items under `#[cfg(test)]` or `#[test]` and binary files are skipped by default, and each has a flag to include it. - **Output sized for an agent's context.** Results are a compact table with paths relative to where you ran it, capped by default at the limits in [Options](#options). When something is cut, the output says how many more matched and suggests raising the cap or narrowing the query. - **Predictable.** The same search on the same files gives the same output, in the same order, every time. A bad pattern fails the whole search with a clear error instead of being quietly dropped. - **Hard to break.** A file with syntax errors is searched for whatever parsed. A pathologically deep file is reported as degraded instead of crashing the search. An unreadable directory doesn't stop the rest of the search. ## Install **Prebuilt binary**, attached to each [GitHub release](https://github.com/orin-dx/monokl/releases) (tag `monokl@`): ``` curl -sL "https://github.com/orin-dx/monokl/releases/download/monokl@/monokl-.tar.gz" | tar -xz ``` Targets: `aarch64-apple-darwin`, `x86_64-apple-darwin`, `aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu`, `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`. **cargo**, built from source: ``` cargo install monokl ``` ## Try it Search a directory (the default is the current one): ``` $ monokl search "format price" src/ search[8]{file,lineStart,lineEnd,nodeKind,parent,symbolSignature,snippet,relevance}: src/utils/format.ts,1,3,function,null,"function formatCurrency(amount: number, currency: string = 'USD'): string","2: return new Intl.NumberFormat('en-US', { style: 'currency', currency }).format(amount);",100 src/utils/validation.ts,8,12,function,null,"function validatePrice(price: number): ValidationResult","9: if (price < 0) return { valid: false, message: 'Price cannot be negative' };\n+1 more",70 src/index.ts,3,3,other,null,null,"3: export { formatCurrency, truncateString } from './utils/format';",23 src/utils/validation.ts,14,14,typeAlias,null,null,"14: export type PriceValidator = (price: number) => ValidationResult;",18 src/components/Button.tsx,11,18,function,null,"function Button({ label, price, onClick, disabled }: ButtonProps)","12: const priceValid = price === undefined || validatePrice(price).valid;\n+1 more",13 src/hooks/useCart.ts,11,25,function,null,function useCart(),"15: const result = validatePrice(item.price);",7 src/hooks/useCart.ts,5,9,interface,null,null,"8: price: number;",7 src/components/Button.tsx,4,9,interface,null,null,"6: price?: number;",7 totalCount: 10 help[1]: "showing 8 of 10; --min-score 0 for the 2 rows below relevance 30, or refine with +term/-term" ``` Each row is one match: where it is (`file`, `lineStart`, `lineEnd`), what it is (`nodeKind`: function, class, method, interface, type alias and so on), what holds it (`parent`), its signature, the lines in it that matched (`snippet`), and its `relevance`: the row's score as a whole percent of the top row's score, so the top row is 100 and a row at 50 scores half as well. Rows are in rank order, best first. `relevance` compares the rows of one query; it is not a number to compare across queries. Output uses [TOON](https://github.com/toon-format/spec), a table format that costs fewer tokens than JSON. **How many rows.** The default output is lean. A row is kept when it scores at least 0.3 times the top row (`--min-score`), which is a `relevance` of 30, the first eight rows are always kept, and at most 20 are printed (`--max-results`), so the cap wins when it is lower than eight. When rows were cut, `totalCount` holds how many matched and the `help` line names the flag that brings them back: `showing 8 of 10; --min-score 0 for the 2 rows below relevance 30, or refine with +term/-term`. To page through rows the cap or the budget left out, add `--offset N`: it skips the first N rows of the same ranking and prints the next page under the same cut and caps, and a help line such as `showing 8 of 31; next: --offset 8, or refine with +term/-term` names the next value. To get the output of earlier versions, which printed up to 50 rows with up to three snippet lines each, run `--min-score 0 --max-results 50 --snippet-lines 3`. A method, a constructor, or a class property holding an arrow function or a function expression gets a row of its own when it spans three lines or more and its class is declared at the top level of the file or exported. So does a method, getter, setter, or a property holding an arrow function or a function expression, of an object literal that is assigned to a top-level `const`, `let` or `var`, or is the `export default` value, also through `as`, `satisfies` or parentheses. See [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md) for how these get built. ## Design tenets **Parse once.** Each file is parsed once per run, by one `LanguageAnalyzer`. Later stages read its `FileAnalysis` and never re-parse. **Every stage is bounded.** File size, line length, nesting, file count and time each have a stated limit, and search keeps no state between runs ([ADR 0004](docs/adr/0004-search-stays-stateless-and-every-stage-has-a-stated-bound.md)). **Token budget is non-negotiable.** `--max-tokens` defaults to 20,000. When output is cut, a `help` line says how many rows were cut. An agent consuming monokl's output should never have to guess whether it's seeing everything. **Determinism.** Ties in score break on file path, line range, kind and code, so the order never depends on the walk or the thread schedule. The exception is a partial result after a timeout. **Arena lifetime containment.** No AST node born from the parser's `Allocator` escapes a per-file `analyze()` call. Every field on `FileAnalysis` is owned. This isn't a style preference. It's what lets a `FileAnalysis` cross threads. **Graceful degradation.** A file with syntax errors still contributes whatever parsed. Not built. When built, tier 1 (`LanguageAnalyzer`, per file) produces and tier 2 (`WorkspaceEnricher`, per workspace) folds, and neither does the other's job. **Planned: content hash is authoritative.** If a parse cache is built, a `blake3` hash of file content is its key, and `mtime` and size are only a fast path. Its `parent` is `class Foo` for a class member and `variable api` for the members of `const api = { ... }` (`other default` for `export default { ... }`), and `nodeKind` is `method`, `constructor` or `property`; `parent` is `null` on every other row. A line that matched inside a member is shown on the member's row only, and the class's or object's row appears when it has a match outside its members, such as its name. Shorter members, members of an anonymous class, of an interface, of an object literal anywhere else (inside a function, a call or `module.exports = { ... }`) and functions nested inside a member are still reached through the row that holds them. The `snippet` is the lines of the block that matched, each with its line number and cut at 160 characters. It shows the first matching line by default, then counts the rest (`+1 more`); `--snippet-lines N` shows up to three. A line is left out when the signature column already shows all of it, wherever it is in the block (the lines of a signature that spans several, or the signature line below a Rust item's attributes or doc comments), so the snippet is `null` when the signature is the only match. A line that says more than the signature stays in, such as a decorator, the start of an arrow function's body or a body on the same line. A code line is shown before a comment or attribute line (a Rust doc comment, a `#[...]` attribute), which is shown only when no code line matched or the line limit leaves room. A Rust signature ends before its `where` clause and says `where …` in its place; a line of the clause that matched is a snippet line, after the code lines. To read the whole block, open the file at `lineStart`–`lineEnd`. Under the table, `help` lines report files that were skipped, degraded (syntax errors, too deep to parse) or read lossily (invalid UTF-8), a partial result, hit lines that were cut, and a query with no positive terms. ## Writing a query | You write | It means | | --- | --- | | `format price` | Code that mentions either word, ranked by how well it matches | | `"format price"` | The exact phrase | | `+cart` | Files must mention `cart` | | `-Button` | Skip files that mention `Button` | | `regex:use[A-Z]\w+` | Lines matching a regular expression | | `regex:"a pattern with spaces"` | A regular expression with whitespace, quoted. `+` and `-` work in front of `regex:` too | | `--exact` | Treat the whole query as one literal, operators and quotes included | Matching ignores case. A `-term` removes whole files, not single results. If one query mixes terms, `+cart -Button` finds code in files that mention `cart` but never `Button`: ``` $ monokl search "+cart -Button" . search[2]{file,lineStart,lineEnd,nodeKind,parent,symbolSignature,snippet,relevance}: src/hooks/useCart.ts,11,25,function,null,function useCart(),"12: const [items, setItems] = useState([]);\n+1 more",100 src/hooks/useCart.ts,5,9,interface,null,null,"5: export interface CartItem {",25 ``` ## Options | Flag | Default | What it does | | --- | --- | --- | | `--min-score FRACTION` | 0.3 | Drop the rows scoring below this fraction of the top row's score, which are the rows whose `relevance` is below 100 times it (a row within half a point of the line rounds up onto it), but never one of the first eight. `0` turns the cut off; `1` keeps only the rows that tie with the top. Outside 0 to 1 is a usage error (exit 2) | | `--max-results N` | 20 | Most results to print. It applies after `--min-score` and wins over its floor of eight rows | | `--offset N` | 0 | Skip the first N rows that pass the cut and print the next page, still bounded by `--max-results` and `--max-tokens`. The cut is measured against the top row of the whole result, so pages of one query do not overlap or skip rows. An offset past the last row prints no rows and a `totalCount`, and exits 0; a non-number is a usage error (exit 2) | | `--max-tokens N` | 20,000 | Most estimated tokens (one per three bytes) across the printed rows. The cut is a prefix in rank order and the output says how many rows were cut | | `--snippet-lines N` | 1 | Most matching lines each row's `snippet` shows, 0 to 3; the rest are counted. `0` prints no snippet, so a variable or type row, which has no signature, shows no declaration text. Above 3 is a usage error (exit 2) | | `--exact` | off | Treat the whole query as one literal term, operators and quotes included | | `--tests` | off | Also search test files: anything under `test/`, `tests/`, `__tests__/` or `spec/`, and `*.test.*` and `*.spec.*` in any searchable extension (`ts`, `tsx`, `js`, `jsx`, `mjs`, `cjs`, `mts`, `cts`). Also searches Rust files named `tests.rs`, `test.rs`, `*_tests.rs` or `*_test.rs` (the usual out-of-line `mod tests;`) and Rust items under `#[cfg(test)]` or `#[test]` | | `--no-ignore` | off | Also search hidden files and files that `.gitignore` or `.ignore` exclude, in the search path or its parent directories | | `--language L` | all | Search one language only: `typescript`, `javascript` or `rust`, chosen by file extension: `.ts .tsx .mts .cts`, `.js .jsx .mjs .cjs` or `.rs`. Any other value is a usage error (exit 2) that lists these three | | `--timeout SECONDS` | 30 | Stop after this many seconds and print what was found so far. `0` means no limit. Fractions are accepted (`0.5`) | ## Limits - **Time.** When `--timeout` expires the output says `partial result: 30 s timeout expired after analyzing 120 of 900 files` (or `searching`, when the text search itself ran out of time). The exit code is still 0. A partial result is the only output that can differ between runs, because which files are reached depends on how fast the machine is. At least one batch of files is always processed, so a very small timeout still returns something. A `-term` exclusion applies only to the files that were reached. The directory walk that lists the files is not interrupted. - **File size.** A file over 4 MiB is not read. The output says `2 files skipped: over 4 MiB: a.ts, b.ts`. Source that large is generated or bundled; reading it costs about 2.5 times its size in memory. - **Nesting.** A file nested deeper than 16,384 levels (TypeScript, JavaScript) or 256 (Rust) is not parsed. The output reports it as degraded. - **Files.** At most 100,000 matching files are examined. The output says how many matched and suggests narrowing the query or path. - **Line length.** Only the first 4,096 bytes of a matching line are kept for matching terms against the line. A longer line still matches as a whole, and the output counts the lines it cut. A required term (`+term`) that appears only past that point in a line is not seen. ## Errors and exit codes - **0:** the search ran, even if nothing matched (you get `search: []`). - **1:** the search failed, for example an invalid regular expression or a directory that doesn't exist. The error is printed on stderr in the same compact format, with the cause. - **2:** the command line itself was wrong. ## Language support | Language | Status | | --- | --- | | TypeScript, JavaScript (`.ts`, `.tsx`, `.js`, `.jsx`, `.mjs`, `.cjs`, `.mts`, `.cts`; not `.d.ts`) | Search works today | | Rust (`.rs`) | Search works today. Functions, structs, unions, enums, traits, type aliases, consts and statics, `macro_rules!` macros and inline modules are blocks, as are `impl` blocks and the methods in them and in traits (when 3 lines or more), item-position macro calls (`thread_local! { ... }`, `lazy_static! { ... }`) and `extern` blocks; modules declared in another file, `use` declarations and `extern crate` are not | | Python, Go, Java | Designed, not built | ## Why Existing code-search-for-agents tools are either fast but fuzzy (grep, embeddings) or precise but heavy (a full language server, a persistent daemon). monokl aims at the middle: real AST parsing without a language server, and no persistent index to keep warm. See [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md) for how, and [PRINCIPLES.md](PRINCIPLES.md) for why. ## Docs | File | Covers | | --- | --- | | [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md) | How it's built, in prose | | [PRINCIPLES.md](PRINCIPLES.md) | Design tenets and non-goals | | [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) | How to work on this repo | | [`docs/spec/`](docs/spec/README.md) | The full specification, including what's still to build | | [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) | Guidance for AI coding agents working in this repo | ## Name Monokl (MON-oh-kl) — from _monocle_, a single precision lens for close examination. The binary is `monokl`. ## License FSL-1.1-MIT — Functional Source License, converting to MIT two years after each release. See [`LICENSE`](LICENSE). # Architecture How `monokl search` is built today, then what is planned. Parts marked "planned" are not in the code. For the full designs, see [`docs/spec/`](docs/spec/README.md); for one subsystem, see [`docs/architecture/`](docs/architecture/README.md). ## Analyze once Every file is parsed once, by a `LanguageAnalyzer`: ``` file text → LanguageAnalyzer::analyze() → FileAnalysis (owned: code blocks, test blocks, parse-error flag, degradation) ``` `FileAnalysis` never borrows from the parser's arena. Everything in it is owned data, so it can be shared across threads via `Arc` and outlive the parse call. This is a hard rule, not a style preference. An `AnalyzerRegistry` gives each file to the first analyzer that claims it. TypeScript and JavaScript use OXC, Rust uses `ra_ap_syntax`. ## The search pipeline `monokl search` runs these stages. Each does less work on fewer candidates than the one before. ```mermaid %%{init: {'theme': 'base', 'themeVariables': {'lineColor': '#64748b', 'edgeLabelBackground': '#f8fafc', 'fontFamily': 'ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif'}}}%% flowchart TB S1["1 · Parse the query
+required / -excluded / bare-optional / #quot;phrase#quot; / regex:pattern"] S2["2 · Canonicalize the search root"] S3["3 · Text search
grep-searcher, the crate ripgrep is built on, over the sorted file walk; stops at the timeout"] S4["4 · Boolean evaluation
drop files missing a required term or containing an excluded one"] S5["5 · Block retrieval
analyze survivors, keep only blocks overlapping a matched line"] S6["6 · BM25 rank — K1=1.5, B=0.5
x node-type boost (functions over modules)
x name-match boost (query words in the declared name)"] S7["7 · Dedup
drop blocks sharing >50% of their bytes with a higher-ranked block in the same file"] S8["8 · Budget
cut by --min-score, --max-results and --max-tokens, with a help line saying how many were cut and which flag brings them back"] S1 --> S2 --> S3 --> S4 --> S5 --> S6 --> S7 --> S8 style S1 fill:#dbeafe,stroke:#2563eb,color:#1e3a8a style S2 fill:#dbeafe,stroke:#2563eb,color:#1e3a8a style S3 fill:#e0e7ff,stroke:#4338ca,color:#312e81 style S4 fill:#e0e7ff,stroke:#4338ca,color:#312e81 style S5 fill:#ede9fe,stroke:#7c3aed,color:#4c1d95 style S6 fill:#d1fae5,stroke:#059669,color:#064e3b style S7 fill:#d1fae5,stroke:#059669,color:#064e3b style S8 fill:#fed7aa,stroke:#ea580c,color:#7c2d12 ``` Stages 1 to 7 are core and cap nothing. Stage 8 and the output format live in the agent layer ([ADR 0003](docs/adr/0003-single-crate-with-core-and-agent-modules.md)), which prints through [michi](https://github.com/orin-dx/michi). Search holds no state between runs ([ADR 0004](docs/adr/0004-search-stays-stateless-and-every-stage-has-a-stated-bound.md)). Each stage has a stated bound: file size, line length, nesting, file count and time. See [Limits](README.md#limits). ## Planned Nothing below is built. Each is a design in `docs/spec/`. - **Cache.** An in-memory and disk cache of per-file analyses, keyed by content hash. Search is stateless today, and the design is in [cache-architecture.md](docs/architecture/cache-architecture.md). - **Workspace index.** A `WorkspaceEnricher` layer would fold per-file analyses into an import graph and a symbol index without re-parsing. It needs the dependency and symbol output that was deleted because no command read it. - **More commands.** `symbols`, `refs`, `definition` and `dependents`, which the index would serve. - **Library session API.** A `Workspace` opened once, with snapshots and provenance, for embedders. See [`08-library-session-api.md`](docs/spec/08-library-session-api.md). - **Per-operation precision.** A `CapabilityPrecision` level per analyzer operation, once a command needs to gate on it. - **More languages.** Python, Go and Java. The registry takes a new analyzer without changing the pipeline. - **Daemon and session mode.** See [daemon-lifetimes.md](docs/architecture/daemon-lifetimes.md). ## What's explicitly out of scope Full list and rationale in [PRINCIPLES.md](PRINCIPLES.md#non-goals). Briefly: - No persistent search index. - No embedding-based retrieval by default. - No stemming. - No in-memory trigram index. - No tree-sitter for TypeScript or JavaScript. - No full [Salsa](https://github.com/salsa-rs/salsa) incremental framework. An open investigation, not ruled out. # Principles What monokl believes, and why. See [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md) for how these get built. ## Design tenets **Parse once.** Each file is parsed once per run, by one `LanguageAnalyzer`. Later stages read its `FileAnalysis` and never re-parse. **Every stage is bounded.** File size, line length, nesting, file count and time each have a stated limit, and search keeps no state between runs ([ADR 0004](docs/adr/0004-search-stays-stateless-and-every-stage-has-a-stated-bound.md)). **Token budget is non-negotiable.** `--max-tokens` defaults to 20,000. When output is cut, a `help` line says how many rows were cut. An agent consuming monokl's output should never have to guess whether it's seeing everything. **Determinism.** Ties in score break on file path, line range, kind and code, so the order never depends on the walk or the thread schedule. Scores round to 6 decimal places to remove floating-point divergence between x86-64 and ARM64. The same query against the same code prints the same output on any machine. The exception is a partial result after a timeout. **Arena lifetime containment.** No AST node born from the parser's `Allocator` escapes a per-file `analyze()` call. Every field on `FileAnalysis` is owned. This isn't a style preference. It's what lets a `FileAnalysis` cross threads. **Graceful degradation.** A file with syntax errors still contributes whatever parsed. A file that is too large, too deep or unreadable is reported in a `help` line and does not abort the search. An unsupported `--language` prints a `help` line, not a crash and not silence. **Planned: aggregate views, not re-scans.** An import graph and a symbol index folded from per-file analyses by a `WorkspaceEnricher`, with `symbols`, `refs` and `definition` on top. Not built. When built, tier 1 (`LanguageAnalyzer`, per file) produces and tier 2 (`WorkspaceEnricher`, per workspace) folds, and neither does the other's job. **Planned: content hash is authoritative.** If a parse cache is built, a `blake3` hash of file content is its key, and `mtime` and size are only a fast path. Not built. ## Non-goals Deliberately not built, and why: - **A persistent on-disk search index** (tantivy-style). Search is stateless today, and a planned parse cache would remember parses, not maintain a standing inverted index. Simpler, and the numbers so far say it's fast enough without one below ~50k files. See [`docs/spec/05-research-and-decisions.md`](docs/spec/05-research-and-decisions.md). - **A full [Salsa](https://github.com/salsa-rs/salsa) incremental-computation framework.** Real precedent exists for using Salsa standalone (Astral's `ty`, Biome), decoupled from rust-analyzer's own query set — this is an open investigation track, not a closed door. - **Embedding-based retrieval by default.** No code-specific evidence it beats lexical + structural signals for single-codebase search, and it would mean either bundling a model or calling a cloud API — both in tension with staying local-first and low-latency. Gate behind an explicit opt-in if it's ever added; don't make it the default posture. - **Stemming.** Code identifiers aren't prose; stemming rules built for English text don't transfer. - **An in-memory trigram index.** Tried, measured, rejected — 600MB–1.2GB resident at scale in an earlier design. The planned `WorkspaceIndex` design lands at roughly 90–140MB at 50k files by comparison. - **Tree-sitter for TypeScript/JavaScript.** OXC is the native, arena-owned, actively-maintained alternative already chosen — no reason to trade that for a generic multi-language parser framework on the one language that has a better option. - **A running agent loop.** monokl is a tool an agent calls, not an agent itself. ## Language coverage isn't uniform, and shouldn't pretend to be A language gets a native parser when it earns that investment — not by default, and not on a fixed roadmap regardless of what the parser ecosystem actually supports. - **TypeScript/JS and Rust** — built. Real, mature native-Rust parsers (OXC, `ra_ap_syntax`). - **Python and Java** — planned, not built. No viable native option exists, checked directly against crates.io, so they would use tree-sitter. - **Go** — planned, not built. `gosyn` is a real, actively-maintained native option. Planned: precision per operation declared through a `CapabilityPrecision` model, so no language is silently assumed to match another. # Contributing By participating in this project, you agree to abide by the [Code of Conduct](./CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md). Found a security issue? See [SECURITY.md](./SECURITY.md) instead of opening a public issue. ## Setup [proto](https://moonrepo.dev/proto) pins the toolchain in `.prototools`; [just](https://just.systems) runs every task. ```bash just setup # install the pinned Rust and moon, install git hooks just install-tools # nextest, llvm-cov, machete, mutants, deny, typos, zizmor ``` ## Recipes | Recipe | What it does | | --- | --- | | `just ci` | Everything CI runs | | `just test` | nextest plus doctests | | `just lint` | `cargo fmt --check` and clippy with `-D warnings`, all features and no default features | | `just doc-check` | `cargo doc` with warnings as errors | | `just coverage` | Line coverage, failing below the justfile's threshold | | `just check-drift` | Fails when a duplicated fact (the Callisto pin) disagrees with its owner | | `just deny` | Licenses, advisories, bans and sources | | `just machete` | Unused dependencies | | `just mutants` | Mutation testing, on demand only | | `just changeset ""` | Record a pending change for the next release (Callisto) | | `just changesets` | Check Callisto config and pending changesets | | `just bench [--repo NAME] [--json PATH]` | p50/p95 wall time, peak RSS and output bytes of `monokl search` against `rg` for six query classes on pinned repos (one large) plus a synthetic stress set; warm cache only, no gates (on demand, needs network) | | `just rg-compare [--terms N] [--min-recall R]` | Whether `monokl search` puts a symbol's declaration in the top files, and how much output it costs against `rg -n`, on pinned public repos, plus 18 multi-word questions with known answers (`scripts/rg-compare.questions`, gated by `--min-question-recall`), 36 held-out questions on fastify, trpc and date-fns scored apart (`--min-heldout-recall`, `--min-heldout-member-recall`, both 0.9), and Rust rows on pinned `fd` (24 pooled, gated by `--min-rust-recall`, 0.9) (on demand, needs network) | | `just agent-cost [--detail] [--json PATH]` | Bytes, estimated tokens and turns of one `monokl search` against a fixed rg-only agent policy on the `rg-compare` rows, and whether the answer is in the first 3 rows; deterministic, report only, no model (on demand, needs network) | | `just verify-release ` | Check a published release: tag, assets, crates.io, attestation, binary | ## Where things stand See [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md#current-state). ## Proposing a change - A spec correction: fix the spec file and add a dated entry to `docs/spec/05-research-and-decisions.md`. - A decision with a credible alternative that is expensive to reverse: write an ADR (`docs/adr/0000-template.md`). - Everything else: a PR with a Conventional Commits title. Conventions are in [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md). Highlights: no `unwrap()`/`expect()`/`panic!()` outside tests, one `thiserror` error enum, owned data out of every parse, `camino` paths, 120-column formatting, and no spec IDs in code. ## Pull requests - CI's aggregate `CI` check must pass: lint, tests on Linux and macOS, MSRV, line coverage, and audit. The same checks run on the merge queue's combined commit and again on every push to main; a red main opens or updates a `ci-red` issue. - Keep a PR to one topic. - A change users can see needs a changeset. Internal changes (tests, CI, docs, refactors) do not. ## Writing a changeset Each changeset becomes one bullet in the changelog. Each version lists its bullets under `Major Changes`, `Minor Changes` and `Patch Changes` headings, below the release date and a compare link. The release PR titles each change by its first line and collapses the rest. - **One topic per file** in `.changeset/`, with `monokl: minor` for a new capability or `monokl: patch` for a fix. - **Entries appear in filename order within their bump heading.** Prefix a filename with `0-` (then `1-`) to make an entry lead its heading. - **Put identifiers, flags and syntax in backticks.** - `just changesets` validates them. The rendered text only shows in the release PR, so read it there before merging. Changesets become the project's changelog, so write them for the people who use it, not for the implementer. - Open with a bold lead-in naming the change as the user sees it, then one line on its value: what they can now do or what changed for them. - When there is more to say, add short bullets in this order: why it matters, how to adopt it (commands, configuration, migration), and limits they will hit. Use sub-bullets for detail. - Group a longer entry under bold labels such as **Upgrading** or **Scripting**. Do not use `#` headings; the changelog supplies those. - Put a breaking change in its own paragraph starting `**Breaking:**` (old behavior, new behavior, what to do), and a step users must take in one starting `**Action:**`. Never inside a bullet: the release PR lists them under "Read before merging" only as paragraphs. A removed or renamed flag, a removed or non-public library item, a changed output shape or value and a library signature change are breaking. - One idea per bullet. Leave out internals unless the user must know them. ## Filing an issue Say what you expected, what happened, and, if it's a spec-vs-reality mismatch, which file in `docs/spec/` you were reading.

# Architecture

Topic docs for monokl's subsystems. Read the one your task touches, not all of them. Each distills the `docs/spec/` sections it cites and the edge-case findings that change what an implementer must do; where code exists, the code and its tests are authoritative and the doc should be kept in step with them.

## Task to file

| You are working on | Read |
| --- | --- |
| `error.rs`, `file_io.rs`, `MonoklError`, any `Result<T>` return | [error-taxonomy.md](error-taxonomy.md) |
| `types.rs`, `Language`, `CodeBlock`, `RankedBlock` | [core-types.md](core-types.md) |
| `query/`, ranking, BM25, tie-breaking, determinism | [query-and-ranking.md](query-and-ranking.md) |
| The in-memory and disk cache, digest vs. mtime (planned, not built; `digest.rs` was deleted unread) | [cache-architecture.md](cache-architecture.md); `Digest` is ADR 0002 |
| `LanguageAnalyzer`, `AnalyzerRegistry` | [language-analyzer-contract.md](language-analyzer-contract.md) |
| Daemon and session mode, `PrecisionUpgrader`, `PrecisionLedger` (not v0.1.0) | [daemon-lifetimes.md](daemon-lifetimes.md) |

## Cross-cutting invariants

- One `thiserror` error enum for the crate, `MonoklError`; file I/O failures are `FileIoError` wrapped transparently.
- `camino::Utf8Path` everywhere a path appears, except where the path is by definition not UTF-8.
- `FxHashMap`/`FxHashSet` for internal hot-path maps; `BTreeMap` for anything serialized, because output order must be deterministic.
- Analyzers return fully owned data. No arena-borrowed AST node outlives the parse.

## Elsewhere

- Decisions with a credible alternative: [`docs/adr/`](../adr/README.md).
- The full spec and its decision log: [`docs/spec/`](../spec/README.md), [`05-research-and-decisions.md`](../spec/05-research-and-decisions.md).
- The edge-case audit these docs draw on: [`07-edge-cases-and-failure-modes.md`](../spec/07-edge-cases-and-failure-modes.md).
# Architecture decision records

Short, dated records of architectural decisions: ones that shape system structure, boundaries, or contracts other code depends on. Not a changelog, not a design doc. Comments, `ARCHITECTURE.md` and `docs/architecture/` explain what the code does.

The spec's own decision log, [`docs/spec/05-research-and-decisions.md`](../spec/05-research-and-decisions.md), records how the spec was reached. ADRs record decisions made since, including any that depart from the spec.

## Index

One line per ADR, with what it guards. Add a line when you add an ADR.

- [1. Keep FileIoError in monokl instead of a shared io-errors crate](0001-file-io-error-lives-in-monokl.md): do not reintroduce a private registry; move `FileIoError` to a shared crate only when a second tool needs it.
- [2. Define Digest in monokl until wisp-contracts exists](0002-digest-lives-in-monokl-until-wisp-contracts.md): `monokl::digest` was deleted unread; if `Digest` returns before `wisp-contracts` ships, define it in monokl with the spec's text and serde form.
- [3. One crate with core and agent modules, not two crates](0003-single-crate-with-core-and-agent-modules.md): `core` never imports `agent`, never serializes result types, never depends on tiktoken or michi; split into crates only for a reason a feature flag can't meet.
- [4. Search stays stateless and every stage has a stated bound](0004-search-stays-stateless-and-every-stage-has-a-stated-bound.md): no index, cache or daemon; every stage's doc comment states its bound; no input-sized stacks, size checked before reading, global `--timeout`, deterministic fold order.

- [5. Hits and blocks are identified by byte spans, and blocks form a tree](0005-hits-and-blocks-are-identified-by-byte-spans-and-blocks-form-a-tree.md): no stage derives ownership, signatures or names from line numbers or text; analyzers emit spans, parent indices and typed names once.

Changing any of these needs a new ADR.

## When to write one

Two gates, both required:

1. **Architectural.** It affects system structure (module or crate boundaries, how components interact), a dependency or technology choice that ripples across the codebase, a data format or contract other code depends on, or a cross-cutting constraint (performance model, correctness discipline, security model).
2. **Expensive to reverse and not obvious from the code.** If it gets reverted in a year, what breaks, and would anyone know why?

If either answer is no, it's not an ADR. A single function's algorithm is a code comment; a bug fix or refactor is a commit message; a naming or style convention belongs in `AGENTS.md` or a lint.

## Format

One file per decision: `docs/adr/NNNN-short-title.md`, numbered sequentially, never reused. Copy `0000-template.md` to start.

- **Never edit history.** If a decision changes, write a new ADR and mark the old one's status `Superseded by NNNN`.
- **Status** is one of `Accepted`, `Superseded by NNNN`, `Deprecated`.
- Keep it to a screen. Put technical depth in `docs/architecture/` and link it.

## Writing it

Write it like you're explaining it to the next engineer over their shoulder. One line per paragraph, no hard wrapping. Sentence-case headers.

- Cut filler. If a sentence means the same without a word, delete the word.
- Banned by default: _leverage, utilize, robust, seamless, cutting-edge, essentially, basically, in order to, it's worth noting, it is important to note, at the end of the day._
- Concrete beats vague. Name the file, the number, the command.
- Active voice. "We chose X because Y."
- Show the trade-off. A decision with no downside is a fact, not a decision.

# Architecture

Topic docs for monokl's subsystems. Read the one your task touches, not all of them. Each distills the `docs/spec/` sections it cites and the edge-case findings that change what an implementer must do; where code exists, the code and its tests are authoritative and the doc should be kept in step with them.

## Task to file

| You are working on | Read |
| --- | --- |
| `error.rs`, `file_io.rs`, `MonoklError`, any `Result<T>` return | [error-taxonomy.md](error-taxonomy.md) |
| `types.rs`, `Language`, `CodeBlock`, `RankedBlock` | [core-types.md](core-types.md) |
| `query/`, ranking, BM25, tie-breaking, determinism | [query-and-ranking.md](query-and-ranking.md) |
| The in-memory and disk cache, digest vs. mtime (planned, not built; `digest.rs` was deleted unread) | [cache-architecture.md](cache-architecture.md); `Digest` is ADR 0002 |
| `LanguageAnalyzer`, `AnalyzerRegistry` | [language-analyzer-contract.md](language-analyzer-contract.md) |
| Daemon and session mode, `PrecisionUpgrader`, `PrecisionLedger` (not v0.1.0) | [daemon-lifetimes.md](daemon-lifetimes.md) |

## Cross-cutting invariants

- One `thiserror` error enum for the crate, `MonoklError`; file I/O failures are `FileIoError` wrapped transparently.
- `camino::Utf8Path` everywhere a path appears, except where the path is by definition not UTF-8.
- `FxHashMap`/`FxHashSet` for internal hot-path maps; `BTreeMap` for anything serialized, because output order must be deterministic.
- Analyzers return fully owned data. No arena-borrowed AST node outlives the parse.

## Elsewhere

- Decisions with a credible alternative: [`docs/adr/`](../adr/README.md).
- The full spec and its decision log: [`docs/spec/`](../spec/README.md), [`05-research-and-decisions.md`](../spec/05-research-and-decisions.md).
- The edge-case audit these docs draw on: [`07-edge-cases-and-failure-modes.md`](../spec/07-edge-cases-and-failure-modes.md).
# Architecture decision records

Short, dated records of architectural decisions: ones that shape system structure, boundaries, or contracts other code depends on. Not a changelog, not a design doc. Comments, `ARCHITECTURE.md` and `docs/architecture/` explain what the code does.

The spec's own decision log, [`docs/spec/05-research-and-decisions.md`](../spec/05-research-and-decisions.md), records how the spec was reached. ADRs record decisions made since, including any that depart from the spec.

## Index

One line per ADR, with what it guards. Add a line when you add an ADR.

- [1. Keep FileIoError in monokl instead of a shared io-errors crate](0001-file-io-error-lives-in-monokl.md): do not reintroduce a private registry; move `FileIoError` to a shared crate only when a second tool needs it.
- [2. Define Digest in monokl until wisp-contracts exists](0002-digest-lives-in-monokl-until-wisp-contracts.md): `monokl::digest` was deleted unread; if `Digest` returns before `wisp-contracts` ships, define it in monokl with the spec's text and serde form.
- [3. One crate with core and agent modules, not two crates](0003-single-crate-with-core-and-agent-modules.md): `core` never imports `agent`, never serializes result types, never depends on tiktoken or michi; split into crates only for a reason a feature flag can't meet.
- [4. Search stays stateless and every stage has a stated bound](0004-search-stays-stateless-and-every-stage-has-a-stated-bound.md): no index, cache or daemon; every stage's doc comment states its bound; no input-sized stacks, size checked before reading, global `--timeout`, deterministic fold order.

- [5. Hits and blocks are identified by byte spans, and blocks form a tree](0005-hits-and-blocks-are-identified-by-byte-spans-and-blocks-form-a-tree.md): no stage derives ownership, signatures or names from line numbers or text; analyzers emit spans, parent indices and typed names once.

Changing any of these needs a new ADR.

## When to write one

Two gates, both required:

1. **Architectural.** It affects system structure (module or crate boundaries, how components interact), a dependency or technology choice that ripples across the codebase, a data format or contract other code depends on, or a cross-cutting constraint (performance model, correctness discipline, security model).
2. **Expensive to reverse and not obvious from the code.** If it gets reverted in a year, what breaks, and would anyone know why?

If either answer is no, it's not an ADR. A single function's algorithm is a code comment; a bug fix or refactor is a commit message; a naming or style convention belongs in `AGENTS.md` or a lint.

## Format

One file per decision: `docs/adr/NNNN-short-title.md`, numbered sequentially, never reused. Copy `0000-template.md` to start.

- **Never edit history.** If a decision changes, write a new ADR and mark the old one's status `Superseded by NNNN`.
- **Status** is one of `Accepted`, `Superseded by NNNN`, `Deprecated`.
- Keep it to a screen. Put technical depth in `docs/architecture/` and link it.

## Writing it

Write it like you're explaining it to the next engineer over their shoulder. One line per paragraph, no hard wrapping. Sentence-case headers.

- Cut filler. If a sentence means the same without a word, delete the word.
- Banned by default: _leverage, utilize, robust, seamless, cutting-edge, essentially, basically, in order to, it's worth noting, it is important to note, at the end of the day._
- Concrete beats vague. Name the file, the number, the command.
- Active voice. "We chose X because Y."
- Show the trade-off. A decision with no downside is a fact, not a decision.

# Query & Ranking — Semantic Model

Source: `docs/spec/01-core-architecture.md` §5 (`query/` — lexer, parser, plan), §8 (`rank/` — bm25, boost, tokenize_doc) and the `search` pipeline stages (§20). `query/`, `rank/`, `dedup.rs` and `text_search.rs` are implemented. Where this doc and the code disagree, the code and its tests win.

Edge-case findings #7, #8, #9, #10, #11 and #21 are resolved (05 §18, §21, §24). Open: #16 (no cap on one term's length).

## Lexer (`query/lexer.rs`)

```rust
pub enum Token { Plus, Minus, RegexPrefix, QuotedString(String), Word(String), Eof }
```

- `+`/`-` become `Plus`/`Minus` only when they begin a token — `read_word` otherwise consumes
  greedily to whitespace, so `foo+bar` is one `Word`, not three tokens.
- `regex:` (case-sensitive) emits `RegexPrefix`; the *next* token is the pattern.
- `"..."` → `QuotedString`; `\"` is the only recognized escape.

## Parser (`query/parser.rs`)

```rust
pub enum Modifier { Required, Excluded, Optional }
pub struct ParsedTerm { pub modifier: Modifier, pub pattern: String, pub is_regex: bool }
pub fn parse(input: &str) -> Result<Vec<ParsedTerm>>
```

- `const LIMIT: usize = 64` — caps **term count**, checked post-loop via
  `MonoklError::TooManyTerms { count, limit }`. Whitespace-only input short-circuits to `Ok(vec![])`
  before the check runs.
- Bare `Word`/`QuotedString` → `Optional`, `pattern = regex::escape(...)`, `is_regex: false`.
- `regex:<word|quoted>` (unprefixed) → `Optional`, `is_regex: true`, pattern used **raw**.
- `+<word|quoted>` / `-<word|quoted>` → `Required`/`Excluded`, `is_regex: false`, escaped.
- `+regex:foo` / `-regex:foo` → `Required`/`Excluded`, `is_regex: true`, pattern used raw (finding #8, closed by 05 §24).

## `QueryPlan` (`query/plan.rs`)

```rust
pub struct QueryPlan { pub terms: Vec<ParsedTerm>, pub required: Vec<usize>,
                        pub excluded: Vec<usize>, pub scored: Vec<usize> /* == Optional */ }
impl QueryPlan {
    pub fn from_terms(terms: Vec<ParsedTerm>) -> Self;
    pub fn search_patterns(&self) -> Vec<&str>;    // required ++ scored, in that order
}
```

`search_patterns()` deliberately omits `excluded` — exclusion terms never drive text search; they
apply as a post-match filter in the pipeline's boolean evaluation stage.

**Exclusion-only queries (finding #21, resolved by 05 §21).** A query with no positive term (`-foo -bar`, or an empty
query) returns no results and one `Skipped` diagnostic saying the query has no positive terms, so it is not mistaken for "matched nothing."

## Ranking (`rank/`)

```rust
pub fn rank_blocks(blocks: Vec<(CodeBlock, Vec<String>)>, query_terms: &[&str], df: &HashMap<...>)
    -> Vec<RankedBlock>
```

Per block: `bm25 = bm25::score(...)`,
`ntype = boost::node_type_boost(block.node_kind)`, `name = boost::name_match_boost(&block, query_terms)`
(1.0 to 7.0, below), **`final_score = round6(bm25 * name * ntype)`**.
Sorted by `final_score` descending, then file, `line_start`, `line_end`, `node_kind` and `code`; 1-based `rank` is
assigned after the sort.

`name_match_boost` (`rank/boost.rs`) compares the query terms `Q` (repeats counted) with `N`, the distinct tokens of the
block's declared name (`CodeBlock.name`, tokenized like a document, so stop words such as the `use` of `useWatch` and the
`from` of `FromRequestParts` are not tokens): `R` is the share of `Q` matched by a token of `N`, `P` the share of `N`
that matches a term of `Q`. A token matches a term when they are equal, or when the token has at least 3 characters and
the term starts with it (`ext` matches `extension`, `req` matches `request`). It never matches by being longer than the
term (`parser` does not match `parse`), and a token of 1 or 2 characters has to equal the term. A prefix match counts at
full weight in `R`, in `P` and in `exact`.
`name = round6(1 + 2 * (R + P / 2) / 1.5 + 4 * exact)`, where `exact` is 1 when `R == 1` and `P == 1`. So a name that
holds none of the terms gets 1.0, a name that holds all of them and nothing else gets 7.0, and the name that says more than
the query (`validatePrice` for `price`) or less (`parse` for `parse other`) lands between. 1.0 for an empty query and for a
block with no name or a name of only stop words. 05 §42 records why this shape and the variants it beat, and §50 the
prefix rule and the variants it beat.

BM25 (`rank/bm25.rs`): `K1 = 1.5`, `B = 0.5`, standard Okapi formula, `round6` to 6dp for
cross-platform f64 stability (`DP = 1_000_000.0`) — keep this rounding.

`node_type_boost` (`rank/boost.rs`): Function 1.5; Class/Method/Constructor 1.4; Interface/Struct
1.3; TypeAlias/Enum 1.2; Variable 1.1; Property/Field/Macro 1.0; Module/Impl 0.9; Other 0.7 (§50 moved Impl from 1.1).

## Dedup and snippets

Both read the byte spans the analyzers fill ([ADR 0005](../adr/0005-hits-and-blocks-are-identified-by-byte-spans-and-blocks-form-a-tree.md)); neither reads line numbers or compares text.

`dedup_blocks` (`dedup.rs`) walks the ranked blocks best first and drops a block that shares more than half of the smaller span's bytes with a block already kept in the same file, then renumbers `rank`. The spans of one analyzed file nest or are disjoint, so this drops a block inside a kept block, equal to it, or holding it, and keeps two blocks that share a line but no byte (`const a = 1; const b = 2;`). A member (a block with a `parent`) never duplicates the top-level block that strictly encloses it, in either rank order. A block with an empty span overlaps nothing. A segment tree over the kept spans' ends keeps the walk near-linear (`tests/scaling.rs`).

The snippet (`output/agent.rs`) shows the matched lines of a block, at most `--snippet-lines` (default 1, up to 3), each cut to 160 characters, with the rest counted (`+2 more`). A matched line is left out when its text lies wholly inside the block's `signature_span`, because the signature column already shows it, except that the signature column of a Rust item ends before its `where` clause (`pub fn f<T>(x: T) -> T where …`, cut by `output/agent.rs` at `CodeBlock.where_start`, which the Rust analyzer takes from the syntax tree; ranking still reads the whole signature), so the lines of the clause after the declaration line are candidates. The shown lines are chosen code lines first: a line that starts with `//`, `/*`, `*/`, `* `, `#[` or `#![` (a doc comment, a block comment, an attribute) or a line inside a where clause comes after every other matched line, so such a line is shown only when too few code lines matched or it is the only match. The chosen lines keep their order in the block, and the ones not chosen are counted. With `--snippet-lines 0` the column is `null`, so a variable or type alias row, which has no signature, shows no declaration text.

## Which rows are printed

`budget.rs` cuts the ranked, deduplicated list in three steps, in this order. Core holds none of them; it returns every ranked block.

1. **Relevance cut** (`--min-score`, default 0.3). Keep the leading rows whose `final_score` is at least `min_score * top`, where `top` is the first row's score. The scores fall down the list, so the kept rows are a prefix. A score equal to the threshold is kept, so rows that tie with the top survive `--min-score 1`. A top score of 0 keeps every row (the threshold is 0). `--min-score 0` turns the cut off.
2. **Floor.** The first eight rows are kept whatever their score, or all of them when there are fewer. The floor lifts the relevance cut only.
3. **Offset** (`--offset`, default 0). Skips that many of the rows the cut kept. The cut is measured against the top row of the whole result, so it is the same whatever the offset, and a page is a slice of one deterministic ranking: pages laid end to end equal one large run. Search stays stateless (ADR 0004): every call re-runs the search, and the offset is the only cursor.
4. **Row cap** (`--max-results`, default 20). Applies to the page and wins over the floor: `--max-results 1` prints one row.
5. **Token cap** (`--max-tokens`, default 20,000). The longest prefix of the page whose printed rows fit; a row larger than the whole cap leaves no rows. It counts the printed rows, so it sees the snippet length, and it does not count the skipped rows.

When any rule dropped rows, or the page starts after the first row, the response is truncated: `totalCount` is the number of ranked blocks and the help line is michi's `showing {returned} of {total}; {guidance}`. The guidance names `next: --offset N` while kept rows remain after the page (`N` is the offset plus the rows returned), `--min-score 0 for the N rows below relevance P` when the cut dropped rows (`P` is 100 times `--min-score`; the same offsets still apply with the cut off). `totalCount` and the `of T` in the line count every match, including the N rows below relevance `P`, so the rows reachable by `--offset` alone are `T - N`; `next:` appears only while some of them remain, so following it never reaches an empty page, and `refine with +term/-term`. An empty page that the caps caused names `--max-results N` or `--max-tokens N` instead, because an offset cannot move past a row that does not fit. An offset at or past the last kept row prints no rows, keeps `totalCount`, exits 0 and says `offset 40 is past the last of 31 rows`. The wording is the output layer's (`truncation_guidance`); core carries `total_blocks_before_truncation`, `blocks_cut_by_relevance`, `offset` and `top_score` only.

## The `relevance` column

A search row ends in `relevance`, an integer from 0 to 100: the row's `final_score` as a percent of `top_score`, the
score of the best row of the whole ranking (so the top row is 100), rounded to the nearest whole number and clamped
to 0..=100. Core holds the float and never renders it: `SearchResponse::top_score` carries the top score, and the
output layer (`output/agent.rs`) computes the percent from that float and the row's own `final_score`, the same
floats the sort and the relevance cut use, never from printed text. `top_score` is of the whole ranking, so a page
after `--offset` measures against the first row of the result and its first row is not 100. A top score that is not
positive has nothing to divide by; every row then ties with the top under the cut, so each shows 100.

It lines up with the cut. A row is kept when `final_score >= min_score * top`, so a kept row shows at least
`100 * min_score` (one within half a point below the line rounds onto it), and the rows the cut dropped show less,
which is why the hint says `below relevance P`. The first 8 rows are kept whatever their score, so rows under `P`
can be printed, and only while fewer than 8 rows reach it. `relevance` compares the rows of one query; the top score
is not comparable across queries (BM25 depends on the corpus), so it is not printed. The columns are
`file,lineStart,lineEnd,nodeKind,parent,symbolSignature,snippet,relevance`; the old `rank` was the row index and is
gone. Why: [05 §52](../spec/05-research-and-decisions.md).

Why these defaults: [05 §46](../spec/05-research-and-decisions.md). To get the output of versions before the change, run `--min-score 0 --max-results 50 --snippet-lines 3`.

## Determinism and bounds

Resolved findings, kept so they are not reopened:

1. **#7 — a bad `regex:` term fails the whole search.** Every term, excluded ones too, compiles before any file is
   read (05 §18).
2. **#9 — total-order tie-break.** The six sort keys above leave no ties, so the order never depends on input order.
3. **#10 — the file walk is sorted by file name**, so the set of files reached under the file ceiling is reproducible.
4. **#11 — resource bounds.** The text search examines at most 100,000 files and keeps counting past it, reads at most
   4 MiB per file and keeps 4096 bytes per line; `--min-score`, `--max-results` and `--max-tokens` cut the output; `--timeout` stops
   the work. See [ADR 0004](../adr/0004-search-stays-stateless-and-every-stage-has-a-stated-bound.md).

Open:

- **#16 — no cap on one term's or the query's length.** `LIMIT = 64` bounds term *count* only. Decide whether a length
  cap is needed, and which error reports it (a sibling to `TooManyTerms`, not a repurposing of it).
# Core Types — Semantic Model

Source: `docs/spec/01-core-architecture.md` §4 ("types.rs — all public types verbatim"). `crates/monokl/src/types.rs`
implements the part of it that search reads. This file states what `types.rs` contains.

None of these types derives `Serialize` or `Deserialize`: wire shapes belong to the output layer. A type with no
caller is not defined (see the decision-log entry "Removed public types nothing builds or consumes" in
`05-research-and-decisions.md`), so the spec's `SearchOptions`, `SearchLimits`, `SymbolsResult`, `DependentsResult`,
`TsconfigMode`, `WorkspaceOptions` and `ExtractRequest` are not in `types.rs` until a command uses them.

## CodeBlock / RankedBlock / ParentContext

```rust
pub struct CodeBlock {
    pub file: Utf8PathBuf,
    pub line_start: usize,
    pub line_end: usize,
    pub node_kind: SymbolKind,
    pub span: Range<usize>,
    pub parent_index: Option<usize>,
    pub name: Option<String>,
    pub code: String,
    pub symbol_signature: Option<String>,
    pub signature_span: Option<Range<usize>>,
    pub where_start: Option<usize>,
    pub matched_lines: Vec<usize>,
    pub parent: Option<ParentContext>,
}

pub struct RankedBlock {
    pub block: CodeBlock,
    pub final_score: f64,
    pub rank: usize,
}

pub struct ParentContext { pub kind: SymbolKind, pub name: String }
```

`RankedBlock` nests its `CodeBlock`; the output layer picks the columns it prints.
`CodeBlock.name` is the identifier the block declares, read from the syntax tree by the analyzer (`Trait for Target` for a trait `impl`); it is `None` for a re-export, an anonymous default export, a destructuring declaration, a macro call and an `extern` block. Ranking reads it for the name boost, and nothing prints it.
`CodeBlock.span` is the byte range of the analyzed source the block covers, so `source[span] == code`. The analyzer receives the file's lossy UTF-8 decoding, so offsets match the file's own bytes only until the first invalid sequence. `CodeBlock.parent_index` is the position of the enclosing block in `FileAnalysis::blocks` followed by `FileAnalysis::test_blocks`; it is `Some` exactly when `parent` is, and the parent is earlier in that order and its span contains the block's. A Rust test member of a non-test `impl` therefore points from `test_blocks` into `blocks`. Hit ownership reads both (`pipeline`, [ADR 0005](../adr/0005-hits-and-blocks-are-identified-by-byte-spans-and-blocks-form-a-tree.md) step 2) and dedup reads `span` (step 3).
`CodeBlock.signature_span` is the byte range of the declaration's head, of which `symbol_signature` is the one-line form: it starts at the first byte after any decorators, attributes and doc comments (so `export` and `pub` are inside it) and ends after the `{` that opens a block body, after the `}` of a body with nothing in it, at the start of an expression body or an initializer, or at the end of a declaration with no body. It is `Some` exactly when `symbol_signature` is and lies inside `span`. The snippet leaves out a matched line whose text lies inside it, apart from the lines of a Rust where clause (see `query-and-ranking.md`). `CodeBlock.where_start` is the offset of the `where` keyword of a Rust declaration's where clause, read from the syntax tree's `WHERE_CLAUSE` node; it lies inside `signature_span`, and it is `None` without a where clause and for TypeScript and JavaScript.
`CodeBlock.parent` is the enclosing class or object literal of a member block and `None` for a top-level block; the analyzer sets it, and the agent output prints it as the `parent` column (`<kind> <name>`).
`final_score` is the only score `RankedBlock` carries, and `SearchResponse::top_score` is the best of them over the whole ranking, which the output layer divides by to print `relevance`; see `query-and-ranking.md` for the ranking algorithm itself, not covered here.

## `Language`

One enum names the languages monokl searches, and `analysis/lang.rs` holds every file fact about them:

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
#[cfg_attr(feature = "cli", derive(clap::ValueEnum))]
#[non_exhaustive]
pub enum Language { TypeScript, JavaScript, Rust }
```

- `Language::of(path)` is the language of a file, `None` for an unsearched extension and for `.d.ts`, `.d.mts` and `.d.cts`.
- `Language::rules()` has the extensions, the excluded suffixes and the test-file names; `is_test_path` adds the test directories.
- The CLI's `--language` flag, the `--language` filter in the pipeline, `LanguageAnalyzer::supports` and `languages`, text search's test-file skip and the rg-compare and bench scripts (through the hidden `monokl language-rules`) all read these rules. Add an extension in `lang.rs` only.
- `LanguageAnalyzer::languages` is a slice because one analyzer can own several languages: `TsAnalyzer` owns `TypeScript` and `JavaScript`.
- A variant exists when a language has an analyzer. `Python` was removed because nothing handled it: `--language python` is a usage error (exit 2) that lists the valid values.

## Diagnostic / DiagnosticKind

```rust
pub struct Diagnostic { pub kind: DiagnosticKind, pub path: Option<Utf8PathBuf>, pub message: String }

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum DiagnosticKind { Degraded, Skipped, Warning, LossyRead }
```

Every result type (today only `SearchResponse`) carries a `diagnostics: Vec<Diagnostic>` field. Per the
edge-case audit, **population of that field is inconsistently specified** — do not assume every
degradation path pushes a `Diagnostic`. Confirmed gaps: `dependents` drops unanalyzable files
with only a `tracing::warn!`, never a `Diagnostic` (07-edge-cases..., Part 1 finding #1); most
Part 2 commands declare the field but never describe it being populated (Part 2 finding #3).
When implementing a command that can degrade, check that command's own spec text for whether
`diagnostics` is actually supposed to be pushed to — don't infer it from the field's existence.

## Minor types (one line each)

- `SymbolKind` — universal (`Function, Method, Constructor, Class, Struct, Enum, Interface, TypeAlias, Property, Field, Variable, Module`) + Rust-only (`Impl, Macro`) + `Other` catch-all. `Copy`.
- `SearchResponse { results: Vec<RankedBlock>, top_score, total_blocks_before_truncation, blocks_cut_by_relevance, offset, truncated, diagnostics }` — top-level `search` command output. Counts and the top score only: the output layer words the truncation hint and prints `relevance` from `top_score`. `blocks_cut_by_relevance` is how many of the blocks left out the relevance cut dropped; the row and token caps dropped the rest, so the hint names the flag that lifts each.
- `LineHit { line_number, text, match_starts }` — internal grep-hit representation only. `match_starts` holds the offsets in `text` (the lossy-decoded line) at which a match starts, as ranges of consecutive offsets; `owned_hits` adds the line's start to get offsets in the analyzed source.

## Types removed until a command reads them

`SymbolEntry`, `Visibility`, `DependencyRecord`, `DependencyBinding`, `DependencyTarget`, `BindingKind`, `ExportRecord`,
`JsxAttribute`, `JsxElementEntry`, `TsData` and `LangData` were built for every file and read by no command, so they
are deleted, along with `FileAnalysis`'s `symbols`, `dependencies`, `exports`, `lang`, `digest`, `profile` and
`source_path` fields, `ParentContext.line`, `CodeBlock.matched_keywords` and `RankedBlock.parent_context` (a copy of
`block.parent`). Search reads `FileAnalysis`'s `blocks`, `test_blocks`, `had_parse_errors` and `degradation` only. A
command that needs one of them restores it with its analyzer output and a reader. When it does, the spec's names
stand: `owner` (not `impl_owner`) on a symbol, and `pub(super)` maps to `Visibility::Module`, with no `Super` variant.

pub enum Token { Plus, Minus, RegexPrefix, QuotedString(String), Word(String), Eof }
```

- `+`/`-` become `Plus`/`Minus` only when they begin a token — `read_word` otherwise consumes
  greedily to whitespace, so `foo+bar` is one `Word`, not three tokens.
- `regex:` (case-sensitive) emits `RegexPrefix`; the *next* token is the pattern.
- `"..."` → `QuotedString`; `\"` is the only recognized escape.

```

## Ranking (`rank/`)

```rust
pub fn rank_blocks(blocks: Vec<(CodeBlock, Vec<String>)>, query_terms: &[&str], df: &HashMap<...>)
    -> Vec<RankedBlock>
```

Per block: `bm25 = bm25::score(...)`,
`ntype = boost::node_type_boost(block.node_kind)`, `name = boost::name_match_boost(&block, query_terms)`
(1.0 to 7.0, below), **`final_score = round6(bm25 * name * ntype)`**.
Sorted by `final_score` descending, then file, `line_start`, `line_end`, `node_kind` and `code`; 1-based `rank` is
assigned after the sort.

`name_match_boost` (`rank/boost.rs`) compares the query terms `Q` (repeats counted) with `N`, the distinct tokens of the
block's declared name (`CodeBlock.name`, tokenized like a document, so stop words such as the `use` of `useWatch` and the
`from` of `FromRequestParts` are not tokens): `R` is the share of `Q` matched by a token of `N`, `P` the share of `N`
that matches a term of `Q`. A token matches a term when they are equal, or when the token has at least 3 characters and
the term starts with it (`ext` matches `extension`, `req` matches `request`). It never matches by being longer than the
term (`parser` does not match `parse`), and a token of 1 or 2 characters has to equal the term. A prefix match counts at
full weight in `R`, in `P` and in `exact`.
`name = round6(1 + 2 * (R + P / 2) / 1.5 + 4 * exact)`, where `exact` is 1 when `R == 1` and `P == 1`. So a name that
holds none of the terms gets 1.0, a name that holds all of them and nothing else gets 7.0, and the name that says more than
the query (`validatePrice` for `price`) or less (`parse` for `parse other`) lands between. 1.0 for an empty query and for a
block with no name or a name of only stop words. 05 §42 records why this shape and the variants it beat, and §50 the
prefix rule and the variants it beat.

BM25 (`rank/bm25.rs`): `K1 = 1.5`, `B = 0.5`, standard Okapi formula, `round6` to 6dp for
cross-platform f64 stability (`DP = 1_000_000.0`) — keep this rounding.

`node_type_boost` (`rank/boost.rs`): Function 1.5; Class/Method/Constructor 1.4; Interface/Struct
1.3; TypeAlias/Enum 1.2; Variable 1.1; Property/Field/Macro 1.0; Module/Impl 0.9; Other 0.7 (§50 moved Impl from 1.1).

## Dedup and snippets

Both read the byte spans the analyzers fill ([ADR 0005](../adr/0005-hits-and-blocks-are-identified-by-byte-spans-and-blocks-form-a-tree.md)); neither reads line numbers or compares text.

`dedup_blocks` (`dedup.rs`) walks the ranked blocks best first and drops a block that shares more than half of the smaller span's bytes with a block already kept in the same file, then renumbers `rank`. The spans of one analyzed file nest or are disjoint, so this drops a block inside a kept block, equal to it, or holding it, and keeps two blocks that share a line but no byte (`const a = 1; const b = 2;`). A member (a block with a `parent`) never duplicates the top-level block that strictly encloses it, in either rank order. A block with an empty span overlaps nothing. A segment tree over the kept spans' ends keeps the walk near-linear (`tests/scaling.rs`).

The snippet (`output/agent.rs`) shows the matched lines of a block, at most `--snippet-lines` (default 1, up to 3), each cut to 160 characters, with the rest counted (`+2 more`). A matched line is left out when its text lies wholly inside the block's `signature_span`, because the signature column already shows it, except that the signature column of a Rust item ends before its `where` clause (`pub fn f<T>(x: T) -> T where …`, cut by `output/agent.rs` at `CodeBlock.where_start`, which the Rust analyzer takes from the syntax tree; ranking still reads the whole signature), so the lines of the clause after the declaration line are candidates. The shown lines are chosen code lines first: a line that starts with `//`, `/*`, `*/`, `* `, `#[` or `#![` (a doc comment, a block comment, an attribute) or a line inside a where clause comes after every other matched line, so such a line is shown only when too few code lines matched or it is the only match. The chosen lines keep their order in the block, and the ones not chosen are counted. With `--snippet-lines 0` the column is `null`, so a variable or type alias row, which has no signature, shows no declaration text.

## Which rows are printed

`budget.rs` cuts the ranked, deduplicated list in three steps, in this order. Core holds none of them; it returns every ranked block.

1. **Relevance cut** (`--min-score`, default 0.3). Keep the leading rows whose `final_score` is at least `min_score * top`, where `top` is the first row's score. The scores fall down the list, so the kept rows are a prefix. A score equal to the threshold is kept, so rows that tie with the top survive `--min-score 1`. A top score of 0 keeps every row (the threshold is 0). `--min-score 0` turns the cut off.
2. **Floor.** The first eight rows are kept whatever their score, or all of them when there are fewer. The floor lifts the relevance cut only.
3. **Offset** (`--offset`, default 0). Skips that many of the rows the cut kept. The cut is measured against the top row of the whole result, so it is the same whatever the offset, and a page is a slice of one deterministic ranking: pages laid end to end equal one large run. Search stays stateless (ADR 0004): every call re-runs the search, and the offset is the only cursor.
4. **Row cap** (`--max-results`, default 20). Applies to the page and wins over the floor: `--max-results 1` prints one row.
5. **Token cap** (`--max-tokens`, default 20,000). The longest prefix of the page whose printed rows fit; a row larger than the whole cap leaves no rows. It counts the printed rows, so it sees the snippet length, and it does not count the skipped rows.

When any rule dropped rows, or the page starts after the first row, the response is truncated: `totalCount` is the number of ranked blocks and the help line is michi's `showing {returned} of {total}; {guidance}`. The guidance names `next: --offset N` while kept rows remain after the page (`N` is the offset plus the rows returned), `--min-score 0 for the N rows below relevance P` when the cut dropped rows (`P` is 100 times `--min-score`; the same offsets still apply with the cut off). `totalCount` and the `of T` in the line count every match, including the N rows below relevance `P`, so the rows reachable by `--offset` alone are `T - N`; `next:` appears only while some of them remain, so following it never reaches an empty page, and `refine with +term/-term`. An empty page that the caps caused names `--max-results N` or `--max-tokens N` instead, because an offset cannot move past a row that does not fit. An offset at or past the last kept row prints no rows, keeps `totalCount`, exits 0 and says `offset 40 is past the last of 31 rows`. The wording is the output layer's (`truncation_guidance`); core carries `total_blocks_before_truncation`, `blocks_cut_by_relevance`, `offset` and `top_score` only.

## The `relevance` column

A search row ends in `relevance`, an integer from 0 to 100: the row's `final_score` as a percent of `top_score`, the
score of the best row of the whole ranking (so the top row is 100), rounded to the nearest whole number and clamped
to 0..=100. Core holds the float and never renders it: `SearchResponse::top_score` carries the top score, and the
output layer (`output/agent.rs`) computes the percent from that float and the row's own `final_score`, the same
floats the sort and the relevance cut use, never from printed text. `top_score` is of the whole ranking, so a page
after `--offset` measures against the first row of the result and its first row is not 100. A top score that is not
positive has nothing to divide by; every row then ties with the top under the cut, so each shows 100.

It lines up with the cut. A row is kept when `final_score >= min_score * top`, so a kept row shows at least
`100 * min_score` (one within half a point below the line rounds onto it), and the rows the cut dropped show less,
which is why the hint says `below relevance P`. The first 8 rows are kept whatever their score, so rows under `P`
can be printed, and only while fewer than 8 rows reach it. `relevance` compares the rows of one query; the top score
is not comparable across queries (BM25 depends on the corpus), so it is not printed. The columns are
`file,lineStart,lineEnd,nodeKind,parent,symbolSignature,snippet,relevance`; the old `rank` was the row index and is
gone. Why: [05 §52](../spec/05-research-and-decisions.md).

Why these defaults: [05 §46](../spec/05-research-and-decisions.md). To get the output of versions before the change, run `--min-score 0 --max-results 50 --snippet-lines 3`.

## Determinism and bounds

Resolved findings, kept so they are not reopened:

1. **#7 — a bad `regex:` term fails the whole search.** Every term, excluded ones too, compiles before any file is
   read (05 §18).
2. **#9 — total-order tie-break.** The six sort keys above leave no ties, so the order never depends on input order.
3. **#10 — the file walk is sorted by file name**, so the set of files reached under the file ceiling is reproducible.
4. **#11 — resource bounds.** The text search examines at most 100,000 files and keeps counting past it, reads at most
   4 MiB per file and keeps 4096 bytes per line; `--min-score`, `--max-results` and `--max-tokens` cut the output; `--timeout` stops
   the work. See [ADR 0004](../adr/0004-search-stays-stateless-and-every-stage-has-a-stated-bound.md).

Open:

- **#16 — no cap on one term's or the query's length.** `LIMIT = 64` bounds term *count* only. Decide whether a length
  cap is needed, and which error reports it (a sibling to `TooManyTerms`, not a repurposing of it).

## CodeBlock / RankedBlock / ParentContext

```rust
pub struct CodeBlock {
    pub file: Utf8PathBuf,
    pub line_start: usize,
    pub line_end: usize,
    pub node_kind: SymbolKind,
    pub span: Range<usize>,
    pub parent_index: Option<usize>,
    pub name: Option<String>,
    pub code: String,
    pub symbol_signature: Option<String>,
    pub signature_span: Option<Range<usize>>,
    pub where_start: Option<usize>,
    pub matched_lines: Vec<usize>,
    pub parent: Option<ParentContext>,
}

pub struct RankedBlock {
    pub block: CodeBlock,
    pub final_score: f64,
    pub rank: usize,
}

pub struct ParentContext { pub kind: SymbolKind, pub name: String }
```

`RankedBlock` nests its `CodeBlock`; the output layer picks the columns it prints.
`CodeBlock.name` is the identifier the block declares, read from the syntax tree by the analyzer (`Trait for Target` for a trait `impl`); it is `None` for a re-export, an anonymous default export, a destructuring declaration, a macro call and an `extern` block. Ranking reads it for the name boost, and nothing prints it.
`CodeBlock.span` is the byte range of the analyzed source the block covers, so `source[span] == code`. The analyzer receives the file's lossy UTF-8 decoding, so offsets match the file's own bytes only until the first invalid sequence. `CodeBlock.parent_index` is the position of the enclosing block in `FileAnalysis::blocks` followed by `FileAnalysis::test_blocks`; it is `Some` exactly when `parent` is, and the parent is earlier in that order and its span contains the block's. A Rust test member of a non-test `impl` therefore points from `test_blocks` into `blocks`. Hit ownership reads both (`pipeline`, [ADR 0005](../adr/0005-hits-and-blocks-are-identified-by-byte-spans-and-blocks-form-a-tree.md) step 2) and dedup reads `span` (step 3).
`CodeBlock.signature_span` is the byte range of the declaration's head, of which `symbol_signature` is the one-line form: it starts at the first byte after any decorators, attributes and doc comments (so `export` and `pub` are inside it) and ends after the `{` that opens a block body, after the `}` of a body with nothing in it, at the start of an expression body or an initializer, or at the end of a declaration with no body. It is `Some` exactly when `symbol_signature` is and lies inside `span`. The snippet leaves out a matched line whose text lies inside it, apart from the lines of a Rust where clause (see `query-and-ranking.md`). `CodeBlock.where_start` is the offset of the `where` keyword of a Rust declaration's where clause, read from the syntax tree's `WHERE_CLAUSE` node; it lies inside `signature_span`, and it is `None` without a where clause and for TypeScript and JavaScript.
`CodeBlock.parent` is the enclosing class or object literal of a member block and `None` for a top-level block; the analyzer sets it, and the agent output prints it as the `parent` column (`<kind> <name>`).
`final_score` is the only score `RankedBlock` carries, and `SearchResponse::top_score` is the best of them over the whole ranking, which the output layer divides by to print `relevance`; see `query-and-ranking.md` for the ranking algorithm itself, not covered here.

# 1. Keep FileIoError in monokl instead of a shared io-errors crate

**Status:** Accepted **Date:** 2026-10-21

## Context

The spec (`01-core-architecture.md` §1 and §27) puts `FileIoError` in a separate `io-errors` crate, pulled from a private `orin-cargo` registry. That crate was never written or published, and no `.cargo/config.toml` defines the registry, so `cargo metadata` failed at manifest parse and monokl could not build or run a single test.

## Decision

`FileIoError` is the `monokl::file_io` module, with the spec's §27 contents unchanged. `MonoklError::Io` wraps it with `#[error(transparent)]` and `#[from]`. There is no private registry: every dependency, michi included (published as `michi-core`), comes from crates.io, and `deny.toml` denies any other source.

## Consequences

- monokl builds and tests with no out-of-repo setup.
- Another orin-dx tool that wants the same type cannot depend on it without depending on monokl. When a second tool needs it, it moves to a shared crate, under michi's own "second independent data point" rule.
- `docs/spec/01-core-architecture.md` §1 and §27 still describe the separate crate and need a matching correction.

## Alternatives considered

- **A new michi crate.** michi renders agent-facing responses; its principles keep domain logic out, and a file I/O error with a path is domain logic. One consumer is also one data point, which michi's principles say is not enough to add a primitive.
- **`crates/io-errors` in this workspace.** It would be publishable on its own, but it adds a crate to version and release for one 70-line enum with one consumer. callisto merged its crates down to four for the same overhead.
# 2. Define Digest in monokl until wisp-contracts exists

**Status:** Accepted **Date:** 2026-10-23

**Update:** `monokl::digest` was deleted unread: no code consumed `Digest`, `FileAnalysis.digest` or the `blake3` and `serde` dependencies it needed. The decision below applies to whoever adds `Digest` back (cache or session work), not to the deleted module.

## Context

`08-library-session-api.md` §8.4 replaces bare-hex `ContentHash` with an algorithm-prefixed `Digest` and places it in `wisp-contracts`, an MIT crate in the Wisp repository. That crate does not exist: it is not on crates.io and the Wisp repository has no such crate. FileAnalysis, the cache and disk persistence all key on the digest, and §14 says nothing should be built on bare hex.

## Decision

`Digest` and `DigestAlgorithm` live in `monokl::digest` with exactly the §8.4 shape: public `algorithm` and `bytes` fields, an exhaustive `DigestAlgorithm { Sha256, Blake3 }` (no `#[non_exhaustive]`), `algorithm:hex` text, lowercase-only hex. When `wisp-contracts` ships `Digest`, monokl re-exports it from `monokl::digest` and deletes its own.

## Consequences

- Cache, FileAnalysis and persistence work can start now on the type they will keep.
- The move is a re-export, not a format change: the text and serde forms are fixed by §8.4, so cache entries written before the move still parse after it.
- Until then the type is FSL-1.1-MIT inside monokl, so a third-party harness plugin cannot link it. Nothing consumes it outside monokl yet.

## Alternatives considered

- **Wait for wisp-contracts.** Blocks tracks 14, 16 and 17 on a crate nobody has started.
- **Keep bare-hex `ContentHash` for now.** §14's warning: every cache entry written would need migrating when `Digest` lands.
